data.name: QualityHeading
data.value: QUALITY

data.name: CustomQualityTip
data.value: Fine settings for custom quality

data.name: QualityLow
data.value: Low

data.name: QualityLowTip
data.value: 720 at most, 30 frames per second, reduced bitrate, and the phone is polled half as often. For modest machines and phones, or many accounts at once.

data.name: QualityMedium
data.value: Medium

data.name: QualityMediumTip
data.value: 1080 at most, 60 frames per second. The original setting, which suits most machines.

data.name: QualityHigh
data.value: High

data.name: QualityHighTip
data.value: Image at the window's resolution, with no cap at all, and double the bitrate. Hard on the phone: keep it for a recent device, and over Wi-Fi for a network that keeps up.

data.name: QualityCustom
data.value: Custom

data.name: QualityCustomTip
data.value: Set the resolution, the frame rate, the image detail and the codec yourself. The three tiers remain the ordinary route: this one is for whoever already knows what they want.

data.name: FineSettingsHeading
data.value: FINE SETTINGS

data.name: MaxResolution
data.value: Max. resolution

data.name: MaxResolutionTip
data.value: A ceiling, not the resolution used: that one follows the window size and can be lower.

data.name: FrameRate
data.value: Frame rate

data.name: ImageDetail
data.value: Image detail

data.name: ImageDetailTip
data.value: Bits granted to each pixel of each frame. The bitrate follows from the resolution actually used, as for the three other tiers: an absolute bitrate would feast a small window and starve a large one.

data.name: VideoCodec
data.value: Video codec

data.name: VideoCodecTip
data.value: AV1 and VP8 are not offered: on an ordinary phone they have no hardware encoder, and encoding them in software costs far more than they give back.

data.name: BitsPerPixelTip
data.value: Bits granted to each pixel of each frame. The trade reference sits around 0.10 for well-made H.264.

data.name: BitrateTip
data.value: What the phone will have to push over Wi-Fi. A Wi-Fi 4 device on 2.4 GHz gives about sixty megabits in practice.

data.name: ResolutionAdviceTip
data.value: The resolution follows the size of your windows. Measured: in a window 1428 tall, going from 1080 to 1440 costs 78 % more bitrate for an image difference of 0.63 out of 255; in a window of 1800, the difference becomes visible.

data.name: GameDistanceHeading
data.value: DISTANCE IN THE GAME

data.name: GameDistanceTip
data.value: Acts on the screen density Android sees, not on the image detail: at equal window size, the game shows more or less ground.

data.name: ZoomVeryFar
data.value: Very far

data.name: ZoomVeryFarTip
data.value: The most ground it is possible to show. The game interface becomes small: on a modest window it will be at the edge of legible.

data.name: ZoomFar
data.value: Far

data.name: ZoomFarTip
data.value: A lot of ground visible, the game interface small. Handy to follow several accounts at a glance, less comfortable to aim.

data.name: ZoomNormal
data.value: Normal

data.name: ZoomNormalTip
data.value: The original setting, that of a 1080 pixel display at 240 dpi.

data.name: ZoomClose
data.value: Close

data.name: ZoomCloseTip
data.value: The least ground possible, the game interface at its largest. Comfortable on a small window. On a window over 2300 pixels tall, this tier draws close to the previous one: the density asked for hits its ceiling there.

data.name: WindowFreezes
data.value: A window freezes after a while

data.name: SleepExplanation
data.value: DT Hub keeps the device's screen on, but Android puts to sleep by itself the applications it judges idle, and a game window that is not in the foreground is one of them. The windows then freeze one after another, the oldest first. One setting is enough to prevent it, and it holds.

data.name: OpenBatterySetting
data.value: 1. Open the game's battery setting

data.name: SettingCalledPrefix
data.value: On this device, the setting to find is called “

data.name: RemoveRestrictions
data.value: 2. Take it out of the restrictions

data.name: RemoveRestrictionsHelp
data.value: The game must be able to run in the background without limit. This is the only handling needed in most cases, and it survives restarts.

data.name: RepeatForEachCopy
data.value: 3. Do it again for each copy of the game

data.name: RepeatForEachCopyHelp
data.value: A cloned application, or one installed in a second profile, is a separate application in Android's eyes: it has its own restrictions, and the setting made on one does not hold for the other.

data.name: AlreadyFrozenHelp
data.value: A window that has already frozen is repaired by restarting it: the “Restart” button on its row restarts the game without closing the window.
